_meta.project: Assa Abloy warehouse redesign @ DHL Bemmel (NL_0032)
_meta.rule: Every externally-sourced or estimated number used in the report must appear here with a source or be labelled an assumption. No fabricated data.

assumptions.assumption: Max facility footprint
assumptions.reason: Given hard project constraint

assumptions.assumption: Max clear/building height
assumptions.reason: Given hard project constraint

assumptions.assumption: Analysis period is representative of normal operation
assumptions.value: Apr-Jun 2025 (Q2)
assumptions.reason: Only 3 months of outbound + 3 storage snapshots were provided; seasonality outside Q2 is unknown

assumptions.assumption: Storage requirement is based on OCCUPIED LOCATIONS (pallet positions), not loads
assumptions.value: peak 8,512 positions (11,015 loads)
assumptions.reason: 11,015 loads sit in 8,512 locations (some locations hold >1 load). Positions, not loads, drive racking. Agreed in class / teacher feedback (Rogier).

assumptions.assumption: STAGED STATUS 'LATE' reflects staging vs the LATE SHIP window, i.e. a genuine on-time-staging miss
assumptions.reason: 50.1% LATE is very high; definition of the threshold must be confirmed before treating as a service failure
assumptions.source: Measured, definition to confirm with DHL

assumptions.assumption: No labour-productivity, MHE-fleet or cost data was provided
assumptions.value: to be sourced
assumptions.reason: Picks/hour, putaway/hour, FTE, MHE counts, CAPEX/OPEX rates are absent; will use benchmarked values with sources and sensitivity analysis
assumptions.source: Gap - external benchmarks + DHL confirmation required

assumptions.assumption: No dedicated inbound/receiving transaction file was provided
assumptions.value: derive proxy
assumptions.reason: Receiving volume will be approximated from ADD DATE / RECEIVE KEY / INBOUND TRUCK NO in storage snapshots and snapshot-to-snapshot inventory growth

assumptions.assumption: The 7,000 m2 / 12.2 m envelope is the space available to DESIGN THE ASSA ABLOY operation within
assumptions.value: 7000 m2 for Assa Abloy
assumptions.reason: Official brief calls 7,000 m2 'the new site', but the site historically served 4 clients (Tiel). If 7,000 m2 is the whole shared building, the Assa Abloy envelope is smaller. Materially changes capacity feasibility.
assumptions.source: Official brief (Project OTM) - to confirm with DHL

assumptions.assumption: Current state = the existing post-move Bemmel layout captured in the storage snapshots (WH NL_0032)
assumptions.value: storage snapshots = current state
assumptions.reason: Brief states the warehouse was recently relocated to Bemmel under time pressure and the current design is believed suboptimal; the provided inventory data is the current Bemmel operation

assumptions.assumption: Design pallet-position target
assumptions.reason: Peak occupied locations 8,512 / 0.90 working utilisation. Replaces the earlier ~14,074 (11,015 loads x 1.15 / 0.90), which the teacher judged indefensible (+5,574 over the ~8,500 peak). Growth (+8.2%/qtr) is absorbed by rack headroom, not by inflating the count.

assumptions.assumption: Rack level pitch and count
assumptions.value: 1.41 m pitch; up to 6-8 levels
assumptions.reason: Measured p90 pallet+load height 1.16 m + 0.25 m beam/clearance; usable height 12.2 - 0.5 top - 0.15 base. MHE reach caps levels per concept.

assumptions.assumption: Aisle widths & location utilisation by concept
assumptions.value: wide 3.7 / reach 3.0 (layout) vs ETV 216i Ast 2.63-2.79 / VNA 1.8 m; util 95/80/97%
assumptions.reason: Standard MHE operating aisles and honeycombing/selectivity losses used in the capacity model
assumptions.source: Reach aisle checked against Jungheinrich ETV 216i data (S006); other concepts industry-standard

assumptions.assumption: Functional (non-storage) areas sized from actual order volume
assumptions.value: receiving 262, loose-container zone 190, outbound 216, packing 450 (incl. 207 m2 small-parts shelving), forward-pick 500, offices 250, returns 180, circulation 450 m2
assumptions.reason: Sized from measured throughput: inbound ~99 loads/day received (peak 167), outbound 17.7 pallets + 225 cartons/day (73% of trailers carry no pallets - parcel-heavy). Detailed layout total = 6,731 m2 = 96% of 7,000 (incl. the 190 m2 loose-container zone added after teacher feedback).
assumptions.source: Derived (capacity_plan.py) from measured throughput; factors are planning assumptions

assumptions.assumption: Labour productivity benchmarks (units/person-hour)
assumptions.value: receiving 25, putaway 20, replen 18, case-pick 80, each-pick 55, pallet-pick 22, pack 45, ship 30
assumptions.reason: No DHL productivity data was provided (A006). Benchmark rates drive the labour plan. Pick-type split is now ORDER-DERIVED (A022), not taken from DHL's pick flags. Loose-container de-stuffing is modelled separately (A019). MUST be replaced with DHL actuals when available.
assumptions.source: Industry benchmark (e.g. Bartholdi & Hackman, Warehouse & Distribution Science) - to validate

assumptions.assumption: Shift & equipment parameters
assumptions.value: 7.5 productive h/FTE/shift; 80% MHE utilisation; single main shift
assumptions.reason: 8h shift less breaks/PF&D; equipment availability allowance. Peak may need overtime or a partial 2nd shift.

assumptions.assumption: Peak-aware slotting: spread fast movers, duplicate extreme SKUs, balance picks/aisle on peak forecast
assumptions.value: A-class 60% of picks -> ~20%/zone if spread across 3 zones; duplicate top ~43 SKUs (15% of picks)
assumptions.reason: During peak, congestion (not walk distance) dominates; clustering fast movers in one golden zone jams it. Spread + duplicate + balance on peak-day pick frequency; validate by 150/200/250% simulation.
assumptions.source: Gadeyne 'How to slot a warehouse during peak season' (S003) + measured pick concentration (peak_slotting.py)

assumptions.assumption: Inbound arrives as 2 shipments per day, direct from Assa Abloy factories
assumptions.reason: Stated by teacher/DHL. Data cross-check: ~99 loads booked in per receiving day (lower bound, 14-day windows before each snapshot), max 167; origins CN, DE, RO, NL, ES, FI... The WMS truck-ID field shows ~8-11 IDs/day, which likely reflects ASN/receipt grouping - kept as a dock-door sensitivity.
assumptions.source: Teacher / DHL (S004) + measured ADD DATE / INBOUND TRUCK NO

assumptions.assumption: Part of inbound arrives LOOSE (floor-loaded sea containers) and is de-stuffed and palletised by hand
assumptions.value: ~41% of loads Asian-origin -> 1 container/day avg, 2 at peak; 2-person crew, 3 h per container (2-4 h sensitivity)
assumptions.reason: Teacher: shipments come in pallets and loose. Asian-origin share (CN/TW/KR/VN) used as the container proxy; largest receipts (70-100 loads, all CN) take 1-3 days to book in, consistent with de-stuffing. Unload-only benchmark 1-2 h for 2 people (S005); +palletising per SKU, heavy cartons -> 3 h. Containers are unpacked in a dedicated 190 m2 loose-container zone at door R1 (teacher feedback); sized from 568 Asian receipts: median 20 loads / 7 SKUs, p75 34 loads / 11 SKUs. Loose-load unloading 2-4 h with a 2-3 person crew (S024).

assumptions.assumption: Dock-door planning parameters
assumptions.value: door utilisation 85%; receiving window 06:00-14:00; dock-on/paperwork 20 min in, 15 min out; 4.3 m door pitch; carrier collection time slots
assumptions.reason: Standard planning values. Outbound doors sized on the busiest hour (p90 9 trailers x 18 min / 0.85 = 3.1 -> 4, +1 spare = 5). Requires carrier time slots: WMS dispatch stamps are batch-closed (60% of afternoon dispatches <2 min apart); without slots up to 8 doors (p90) would be needed; today's all-day drop-trailer practice holds ~15 trailers.
assumptions.source: Planning assumption + measured outbound trailer data

assumptions.assumption: MHE cycle-time model parameters
assumptions.value: ETV 216i travel 11 km/h + 4.6 s accel per leg; fixed handling 45 s; mean fork height 5.1 m; ERE 225 at 50% of 14 km/h on dock legs; MHE utilisation 80%; single-deep racks (no telescopic forks)
assumptions.reason: Speeds, lift/lower/reach rates and acceleration from Jungheinrich data (S006-S008); handling allowances are assumptions. Racks are single-deep back-to-back, so standard forks are used (the earlier telescopic-fork time and residual-capacity question no longer apply). Fleet rule (D3): no spare once a type has 2+ units; ERE 225 one per dock side. ECE 225 dropped (too long for 3 m aisles).

assumptions.assumption: Pick type is derived from what the client ordered, not from DHL's historical pick flags
assumptions.value: 75% each / 24% case / 1% full-pallet lines (61% of units are case, 26% each, 13% full pallet)
assumptions.reason: Teacher feedback (Rogier): past DHL pick choices may not be optimal. Each line is classed by comparing PICKED QTY to the SKU's pallet qty (PA QTY) and case qty (CS QTY). Lines without master data (2.3%) are treated as each (slowest, conservative). Also removes the 20% unlabelled 'Other' class.
assumptions.source: Measured (outbound lines x storage master) + teacher feedback

assumptions.assumption: The 08:00 pick peak is caused by the order-release routine, not by when customers order
assumptions.value: 55% of orders arrive 15:00-17:00, ~43% released 16:00-18:00, picked next morning; 08:00 = 1.31x the mean active hour
assumptions.reason: Teacher statement confirmed by ORDER ARRIVE / ALOCATE / PICK timestamps. Future state releases work in waves through the shift (levelling could free ~24% of peak-hour picker capacity).

assumptions.assumption: Picking is split by ORDER SIZE computed from SKU each-dimensions and weights
assumptions.value: small = <=160 L and <=60 kg (4 totes of 40 L / 15 kg) -> trolley; larger -> pick-to-pallet; full-pallet lines -> reach truck
assumptions.reason: Median order is 7 L; 75% fit one tote, 89% fit 4 totes, but the largest orders carry ~88% of the volume. Tote 600x400 ~40 L usable, <=15 kg per tote for manual handling; trolley 6 totes, filled to 80% of volume/weight (S011).
assumptions.source: Measured (outbound x storage master) + design assumption

assumptions.assumption: Pick-time model parameters
assumptions.value: walk 0.8 m/s with trolley; EJE 120i at 65% of 5.6 km/h; 25 s per small-order line, 40 s per large-order line; setup 90 / 180 s per tour; +10% delays; 3 waves/day
assumptions.reason: Travel computed on the Option B layout (return route in the fast-pick area, S-shape in the reserve aisles); handling times are planning assumptions to validate with DHL time studies (A006).
assumptions.source: Layout geometry + EJE data (S010) + planning assumption

assumptions.assumption: Loose containers are unpacked in a dedicated zone at door R1 - by a DHL crew or an on-site contractor, whichever is cheaper
assumptions.value: in-house ~EUR 179 per container (2 people x 3 h x EUR 28 + paid breaks); contractor only if its fixed fee per container is lower
assumptions.reason: Teacher feedback: separate zone for loose containers. Contractors quote a fixed price per container based on weight, number of cartons and stacking pattern (S024); no public price, so the in-house cost is the break-even for a quote.

assumptions.assumption: Trailer departure plan with booked carrier time slots
assumptions.value: 14 trailer slots over 13 departure times/day (25-min windows) at the carriers' current median times; 3 pick waves planned backwards (06:00, 09:30, 12:45)
assumptions.reason: Teacher: 'make a plan on when you want them to leave'. Slots built from each carrier's median departure time (data); max 4 of 5 doors busy at once. Carriers must accept the slots (A020).
assumptions.source: Measured outbound trailer data + planning assumption

assumptions.assumption: Hazardous SKUs: hazard class unknown - PGS 15 (packaged hazardous substances) or PGS 37 (lithium batteries) to be confirmed
assumptions.value: 138 SKUs, 2,197 loads (19.9% of loads), ~385 t gross product weight (01-06-2025; same method in every snapshot: 1,727 / 1,895 / 2,197 loads)
assumptions.reason: Recounted per unique load (LODNUM) with HAZMAT = 1; weight = qty x unit weight. By customs code 95% of hazardous loads are safes (8303), electronic locks (8301), readers (8471), alarms (8531) and cameras (8525) - most likely lithium cells built into the products (UN3481/UN3091, class 9), so PGS 37-2 (lithium energy carriers, from 333 kg, group 1 from 1,000 kg per fire compartment, S029) applies rather than PGS 15. A few loads are lubricants (3403, possibly PGS 15) and loose batteries (8507); 33 loads of cardboard boxes (4819) look like a wrong flag. Gross weight overstates the battery content. Classes to confirm with Assa Abloy (SDS / UN numbers).
assumptions.source: Measured (storage HAZMAT + COMPONENT CODE) + PGS 37-2 (S029) + PGS 15 (S016)

assumptions.assumption: Layout concept: flow-through kept after evaluating a U-shaped alternative (W3 method)
assumptions.value: U-shaped: -9% put-away travel (~10 reach-truck min/day), ~6 vs 8 doors only if all inbound arrives before noon
assumptions.reason: Huertas et al. (2007) favour U-shaped for strong-ABC sites; our picking travel is identical in both (packing east) and C items bring 46% of inbound loads, so the gain is small; flow-through separates inbound, returns and outbound.

assumptions.assumption: Labour cost per paid hour
assumptions.value: operative EUR 20 (high case EUR 28); team leader EUR 27; admin EUR 24
assumptions.reason: Teacher feedback (S026): EUR 20 per hour for a warehouse operator; EUR 28 = CAO wage x employer factors kept as the high case

assumptions.assumption: Working days per year
assumptions.reason: 61 operating days measured in Q2 2025 x 4

assumptions.assumption: Indirect staff
assumptions.value: 1.5 FTE (1 team leader + 0.5 inventory control / WMS admin)
assumptions.reason: Span of control ~1:9 at the peak; not in the data

assumptions.assumption: Racking prices
assumptions.value: EUR 130 per installed single-deep position (80-200); long-goods position EUR 160; protection 5% of racking; re-use of existing racking EUR 25/position
assumptions.reason: EU selective racking EUR 80-140 per position + 30-50% installation

assumptions.assumption: Carton-flow bay price
assumptions.reason: New USD 1,200-2,500 per bay at ~0.9 EUR/USD; used EUR 650

assumptions.assumption: Put-to-light wall
assumptions.value: EUR 150 per slot + EUR 12,000 installation and WMS link
assumptions.reason: USD 60-200 per station; integration USD 3,000-18,000

assumptions.assumption: Small equipment prices
assumptions.value: RF terminal EUR 1,500; trolley EUR 433; tote EUR 16; wrapper EUR 3,849; roller conveyor EUR 1,250; pack station EUR 2,500; roll cage EUR 150
assumptions.reason: Public listings; pack station and roll cage are assumptions

assumptions.assumption: WMS set-up and contingency
assumptions.value: WMS set-up EUR 25,000; contingency 10% of CAPEX
assumptions.reason: ~25 consultant days for waves, put-wall, slotting and putaway rules

assumptions.assumption: Truck full-service lease per month
assumptions.reason: Dutch reach-truck lease and rental offers; Jungheinrich has no public price list - quote needed

assumptions.assumption: Truck energy
assumptions.value: ETV 4 kWh per operating hour, pallet trucks 1.5 kWh/h; EUR 0.2046 per kWh
assumptions.reason: NL non-household electricity price H1 2025

assumptions.assumption: Upkeep
assumptions.value: rack inspection + repairs EUR 2,500/yr; IT support 15% of IT CAPEX/yr
assumptions.reason: EN 15635 yearly expert inspection; no public price

assumptions.assumption: Depreciation
assumptions.value: racking 15 yrs, equipment 7 yrs, IT 5 yrs, straight-line
assumptions.reason: Common accounting lives

assumptions.assumption: Small parts move from pallet racks to bin shelving
assumptions.value: 2,657 slow SKUs (C or no demand) with stock <= 50 L, unit <= 20 L, <= 15 kg, <= 60 cm -> 3,424 half-bins on 188 shelving bays (207 m2) next to the put-wall; frees 1,005 rack locations; 50 lines/h
assumptions.reason: Feedback: store small items efficiently. Kardex Shuttle XP 500 compared: 3 lifts, 66 m2, 75 lines/h but ~EUR 19k/yr more and busy ~6% of the day at 93 lines/day -> upgrade path, not needed now

assumptions.assumption: Maximum real item / pallet length
assumptions.value: 2.05 m (XLONG pallet); 115 loads recorded longer are data errors (e.g. a 10.95 m item of 0.5 kg)
assumptions.reason: Teacher: nothing larger than a door (~2 m) comes in. Long goods in a module with 4.5 m bays (2 pallets each) behind a 3.2 m aisle: a 2.05 m load crosswise needs Ast 2,976 mm (VDI formula on ETV 216i data, S006)

assumptions.assumption: Big containers borrow door R2
assumptions.value: on container days with > ~12 SKUs the north half of receiving (131 m2) beside R2 is used for unpacking; 91% of containers fit the zone alone, 97% with R2
assumptions.reason: Receiving staging peaks at ~17 pallets (~80 m2) because 2 ETVs put away while unloading; 2 doors (R1 + R3) still cover the base and peak scenarios

assumptions.assumption: Area check outbound staging and packing
assumptions.value: outbound staging need: p90 60 m2, max 100 m2 of 216; packing need 423 m2 of 450 incl. shelving and the put-wall
assumptions.reason: Measured afternoon trailers (pallets x 1.9 m2 + roll cages x 1.0 m2, +30%); pack stations, put-wall, shelving, waiting pallets, wrapper, packaging stock

assumptions.assumption: Every fast mover (A/B item) gets a pick face in the fast-pick area
assumptions.value: 31 carton-flow bays (2 m, 5 levels x 6 lanes = 930 lanes) hold the 888 most-picked A/B items that fit a lane (each <= 28 x 33 x 60 cm, <= 15 kg) + 42 second lanes for the top 1%; across the 2.6 m pick aisle a wall row holds the rest: 26 shelving bays (462 items), 5 long-item bays of 2.2 m (42 items up to ~2 m, lying lengthwise) and 20 floor pallet faces (17 heavy/bulky items) = 55 of 63.6 m
assumptions.reason: Check of the design: 1,409 A/B items were picked in Q2 but the carton flow has 930 lanes. Lanes go to the items with the most picks (89.5% of fast-pick lines); the rest face the same aisle, so the pick walk does not change. Lane and shelf sizes are planning assumptions; shelving priced as the small-parts shelving (S030)
assumptions.source: Measured (Q2 order lines, SKU dimensions) + planning assumption + S030

assumptions.assumption: Fixed places inside the working zones
assumptions.value: Receiving: R2 in the north half (lent to container unpacking on big-container days), R3 in the south half; container zone: 10.5 m roller conveyor from R1, 12 build spots (6 each side), 35-pallet buffer, 4 x 4 m wrap/label station; fast-pick band: wall row 1.2 m, pick aisle 2.6 m, carton flow 1.8 m deep, refill strip ~1.6 m
assumptions.reason: Drawn to scale in geometry.py so the floor plan, the zone figures and the space checks (dock_mhe_plan.py) use the same places; sizes follow the parts sized in A013, A044 and A046
